title: Thermal-Aware Spot Instance Coordinator and Tenant SLA Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========
This runbook defines the operational procedure for coordinating spot (preemptible) instance pools in the GPU fleet while respecting thermal budgets and tenant SLAs. It clarifies automated coordinator behavior, operator actions for emergent thermal events, dashboard and alert thresholds, and the decision matrix for safe tenant rebalancing and preemption.

Purpose
-------
- Reduce unplanned tenant impact when nodes are thermally constrained or preempted.
- Ensure predictable degradation policies that preserve high-priority SLAs.
- Provide clear operator steps for mitigation, rollback, and customer communication.

Scope
-----
This document applies to:
- Multi-tenant GPU clusters that combine on-demand and spot/preemptible nodes.
- Services with tiered SLAs (gold/silver/bronze).
- Thermal throttling events originating from chassis-level sensors, rack PDU limits, or cloud provider thermal-driven live shrink.
It does NOT cover kernel-level GPU driver failures, software OOM, or network partitioning (see the incident-runbooks directory for those).

Owners and Contacts
-------------------
- Primary owner: Platform Capacity (oncall) — rotation: platform-op@redwood.com
- Secondary owner: GPU Fleet Team — lead: Marco Alvarez
- Pager: #platform-oncall channel

Definitions
-----------
- Thermal event: any condition where chassis/rack/gpu thermal metrics exceed configured safe thresholds causing either automatic GPU frequency scaling or provider-initiated node withdrawal.
- Spot coordinator: the runtime component that decides which spot instances to preempt/shed and which tenants to migrate among hybrid pools.
- Priority tier: gold/silver/bronze as defined in tenant contracts.

SLOs and Business Rules
------------------------
- Gold tenants: 99.95% availability, max degraded latency 200ms for 90th pct tail.
- Silver tenants: 99.5% availability, max degraded latency 300ms.
- Bronze tenants: 98% availability; best-effort during thermal events.
- Platform must avoid gold tenant preemption unless: (a) entire region thermal hazard > 90% and (b) operator-approved emergency diversion.

Decision Matrix (high-level)
---------------------------
Use the matrix below to decide action for a given thermal severity and spot pool state:

| Thermal Severity | Spot Spare Capacity | Preferred Action | Operator Note |
|------------------|---------------------|------------------|---------------|
| Low (<65%) | >15% | No action; prefetch cooling hints | Monitor for upward trend |
| Moderate (65-80%) | 5-15% | Evict bronze tenants on oldest allocations; enable preemptible draining | Notify tenants if eviction > 12 mins |
| High (80-95%) | <5% | Suspend new spot placements; migrate silver to dedicated if credits allow; evacuate vulnerable nodes | Initiate cross-region spill if policy allows |
| Critical (>95%) | 0% | Emergency throttle: force drain and manual gold-protect; consider temporary paid-burst purchases | Escalate to SRE lead |

Observability: dashboards and alerts
----------------------------------
Dashboards required:
- Fleet thermal heatmap (per rack, per AZ) with 1m and 15m aggregates.
- Spot spare capacity gauge by region and GPU family.
- Tenant degradation SLI panel: request latency, error-rate, token gap.

Key alerts (examples with thresholds):
1) thermal.region.high — fires when avg GPU chassis temp > 80C for 5m. Severity: P1. Pager to oncall.
2) spot.spare.low — spare capacity < 5% for 10m. Severity: P2. Slack notification + runbook link.
3) tenant.degradation.gold — gold tenant latency > 200ms 90th for 10m. Severity: P1. Customer telephony escalation.

Alert handling SLA: acknowledge within 5 minutes for P1 and start mitigation within 15 minutes.

Operator Runbook (step-by-step)
-------------------------------
Precondition: Confirm thermal alert and that no unrelated incidents are causing false positives (power work, scheduled maintenance).

1) Triage (0-10 mins)
   a) Open the thermal heatmap dashboard and confirm affected racks/AZs.
   b) Correlate with cloud provider event stream (if cloud-hosted) or chassis PDUs.
   c) Check spot spare capacity and recent eviction logs (kubectl + coordinator logs).
   Commands:
   - curl -sS https://internal-metrics/api/heatmap?region=us-west-2
   - kubectl -n platform logs deploy/spot-coordinator --since=15m | tail -n 200

2) Quick mitigation (10-30 mins)
   a) If Severity is Low: set coordinator to "cooling-hints" mode to reduce new spot allocations.
   CLI: platformctl spot-coordinator set-mode cooling-hints --region us-west-2
   b) If Moderate: trigger graceful eviction policy for bronze tenants: platformctl spot-coordinator evict --policy bronze-oldest --grace-period 300s
   c) If High/Critical: enable cross-region spill and pause all new spot schedules:
   - platformctl spot-coordinator set-mode emergency-pause --region us-west-2
   - platformctl migration start-spill --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --policy gold-protect

3) Gold protection steps (if gold tenants are at risk)
   a) Engage SRE lead and request temporary dedicated capacity reservation for affected gold tenants: platformctl capacity reserve --tier gold --nodes 4 --region us-west-2
   b) If reservation is not possible within 20 minutes, enact customer-facing mitigations: reduce model seq_len limits, enforce token rate-limits at API gateway (see API rate-limiting guide).

4) Communication and customer impact
   - Post an update to #customer-impact with templated message (see Communication Templates section).
   - If degradation crosses contractual thresholds, contact success manager for QBR follow-up.

5) Recovery and verification
   a) After thermal metrics return to <65% for 10m, set coordinator back to normal mode: platformctl spot-coordinator set-mode normal
   b) Verify that evicted bronze workloads are eligible for reallocation and that spot spare capacity returns to >15%.
   c) Run post-event regression checks for token cost spikes and SLI regressions (automated regression job).

Configuration examples
----------------------
Example coordinator YAML (annotated):

apiVersion: platform/v1
kind: SpotCoordinatorConfig
metadata:
  name: us-west-2-thermal-policy
spec:
  thermalThresholds:
    coolingHint: 65
    moderate: 80
    high: 90
    critical: 95
  evictionPolicies:
    bronze-oldest: { graceSeconds: 300, maxParallelEvictions: 20 }
    silver-protect: { graceSeconds: 120, maxParallelEvictions: 8 }
  crossRegionSpill: { enabled: true, maxConcurrent: 3 }

Operator CLI quick-reference
---------------------------
- Check heatmap: platformctl metrics heatmap --region us-west-2 --window 15m
- Set coordinator mode: platformctl spot-coordinator set-mode emergency-pause --region <region>
- Start spill: platformctl migration start-spill --from <region> --to <region> --policy gold-protect

Testing and practice drills
--------------------------
- Quarterly tabletop: simulate a high thermal event during Black Friday load. Validate decision matrix and communications.
- Canary test: schedule a controlled 15-minute thermal-mode switch on a small sacrificial rack to validate eviction pipelines.

Retrospective triggers and metrics to collect
-------------------------------------------
- Any event that caused gold tenant unplanned degradation > 15 minutes triggers a retrospective.
- Metrics to collect: rack temp timeline, coordinator decisions (eviction timestamps, policies applied), tenant SLI trajectories, cost of emergency capacity purchases, time-to-restore.

Post-incident checklist (30-90 mins after restore)
------------------------------------------------
1) Create incident summary in the incident tracker with links to dashboards and logs.
2) Tag affected customers and schedule a QBR action if contractual threshold breached.
3) Propose follow-up work (e.g., increase rack cooling, shift placement heuristics, add thermal-safety prefetch).

Templates and artifacts
---------------------
- Communication template (Slack/email)
  Subject: [Platform] Thermal event in us-west-2 — impact to Bronze tier workloads
  Body: Short summary, time window, customer tier impact, mitigation steps taken, expected follow up.

- Example Grafana query for heatmap panel:
  SELECT avg(temp_c) FROM gpu_chassis_temps WHERE region='us-west-2' AND time > now() - 15m GROUP BY rack

Security and compliance notes
-----------------------------
- Any cross-region spill that moves tenant data must comply with tenant data residency settings. The coordinator respects per-tenant residency tags; operator must confirm before initiating manual spill for restricted tenants.
